## Project summary

A personal **Telegram bot written in Python** that analyzes your **heart rate variability (HRV)** data daily, retrieved via the **Fitbit API**, and sends **training recommendations** based on your physiological readiness.

[View the repository on Github](https://github.com/anna-pirogova/fitbit-hrv-telegram-bot)

<img src="/images/telegram_bot_message_example1.png" width="50%">
<img src="/images/telegram_bot_message_example2.png" width="50%">

## What does the bot do?

- Extracts HRV (RMSSD) data from your Fitbit device  
- Compares it with your personal baseline and calculates deviations  
- Sends a Telegram message with interpretation:
  - Daytime and nighttime RMSSD
  - Metric deviations from baseline
  - Training recommendation: normal workout, intense session, or rest day

> All calculations and message texts can be easily customized in the Python script.

## What you need to run it

### Required:
- A Fitbit or Google Pixel Watch (Gen 1–4)
- A Fitbit Developer Account
- A registered personal app in the Fitbit portal
- Python 3 installed
- A Telegram bot (created via [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather))

### Optional (for automatic notifications right after waking up):
- A verified **subscriber** and **subscription** for sleep events in the Fitbit Web API
- A public domain with HTTPS (e.g., via [DuckDNS](https://www.duckdns.org/))
- A valid HTTPS certificate (via `certbot`)
- A server with a **listener service** (webhook) to receive events from Fitbit

For setup instructions, see the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/anna-pirogova/fitbit-hrv-telegram-bot)
